papers.what_it_is: A Quantum Computing Inc educational web page relating neural networks to the reservoir computing paradigm and arguing that reservoir computing reduces training cost.

assertions.value: The page states that artificial neural networks are an artificial intelligence paradigm loosely inspired by how biological neural networks work, and calls the comparison a vast oversimplification that is conceptually accurate at a very abstract level.
quotes: Artificial neural networks are an artificial intelligence paradigm that is loosely inspired by how biological neural networks work naturally.
This is, of course, a vast oversimplification of how brains and learning work but conceptually accurate at a very abstract level.
assertions.certainty_reason: An educational statement without evidence in the page.

assertions.value: The company states that most implementations of reservoir computers, including its own, can be viewed as types of artificial neural networks, and that recurrent neural networks are the class many reservoir systems formally belong to.
assertions.anchor: Introduction and Training sections, web page
quotes: Most implementations of reservoir computers, including ours, can be viewed as types of artificial neural networks.
Recurrent neural networks (RNNs), the class of neural networks that many reservoir systems formally belong to
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describing its own product class.

assertions.value: The page states that tensors used in machine learning are a special case of mathematics and physics tensors, behave like matrices or vectors given extra dimensions for bookkeeping, and have linear mathematics, whereas mathematics and physics tensors of dimension three or higher can represent non-linear interactions.
assertions.anchor: Linear operations and tensors section, web page
quotes: In mathematics and physics a tensor with dimension three or higher can be used to represent non-linear interactions
machine learning tensors are more like matrices or vectors which have been given more dimensions for bookkeeping purposes, but their mathematics is linear.
The tensor mathematics used in machine learning can be considered to be a special case of math/physics tensors where nonlinearity is avoided.
assertions.certainty_reason: An explanatory statement on a vendor web page, not proved there.

assertions.value: The page defines the basic linear operations in neural networks as adding and subtracting numbers, possibly weighted, and says any set of linear equations can be represented as a matrix.
assertions.anchor: Linear operations and tensors section, web page
quotes: The basic operations to move this information around are known as linear operations, adding and subtracting numbers, possibly in a weighted way
Any set of linear equations can be represented as a matrix, a two-dimensional array of numbers
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states its own definition of linear operations in the Linear operations and tensors section.

assertions.value: The page states that a purely linear neural network, of any size, can be collapsed into a set of linear equations giving the outputs in terms of the inputs, so it needs some nonlinearity to reliably perform sophisticated tasks.
quotes: if we build a purely linear neural network, no matter how big it is, it can always just be collapsed into a set of linear equations describing the outputs in terms of the inputs.
For an artificial neural network to be able to reliably perform sophisticated tasks like recognizing cats, it needs some nonlinearity.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated informally without a proof in the page.

assertions.value: The page describes a rectified linear unit (ReLU) as a node that sets its input to zero if it is negative and leaves it unchanged if it is positive, and says almost any form of nonlinearity can in principle supply the needed complexity.
quotes: a rectified linear unit (ReLU) simply sets its input to zero if it is negative and leaves it as it is if it is positive.
In principle, it seems that almost any form of nonlinearity can introduce the level of complexity we need
assertions.certainty_reason: The page gives its own definition of ReLU in the Nonlinear nodes section.

assertions.value: The page states, with a link to other work, that this generality in nonlinearity has been made rigorous: a shallow neural network with any of a very general class of nonlinear functions can approximate arbitrary mathematical functions.
quotes: This generality in nonlinearity has been made rigorous; a shallow neural network with any of a very general class of nonlinear functions is capable of approximating arbitrary mathematical functions
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited result; the page gives no statement of conditions.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer does not carry the link target, so the cited work is not identified here.

assertions.value: The page states that a ReLU node strongly biased to negative values always returns zero and is then effectively removed from the network.
quotes: the very simplified ReLU node we mentioned before is no longer useful if it is strongly biased to negative values in a way that it always returns a zero value.
In this way, it is effectively removed from the network.
assertions.certainty_reason: An explanatory example without evidence in the page.

assertions.value: The page states that biological neural networks contain strong nonlinearity through the action potential, which gives a strong signal if a threshold is reached and essentially none otherwise.
quotes: Biological neural networks also contain strong degrees of nonlinearity, which comes through the action potential
which leads to a strong signal if a threshold is reached, but sends essentially no signal otherwise.
assertions.certainty_reason: A general statement without evidence in the page.

assertions.value: The page states that training is usually done by defining a loss function that measures network performance and then determining how to change the weights to reduce it, that the weights cannot be derived mathematically, and that the process is computationally expensive and often difficult to implement.
quotes: training is usually done by developing a mathematical function to determine how well the network performs (a loss function), and then determining how to change the weights to reduce the value of the loss function.
there is no way to just mathematically derive what the values of the different terms (known as weights) should be.
The learning process is usually computationally expensive and often difficult to implement.
assertions.certainty_reason: A general description without evidence in the page.

assertions.value: The page states that deeper networks tend to do better on more complex tasks but also become harder to train, and that deep networks need larger training sets or they can overfit by memorizing random statistical fluctuations.
quotes: deeper networks, with more layers of nodes between the input (what is being learned) and the outputs (the conclusions the network returns to the users), tend to be able to do better on more complex tasks.
However, as a network gets deeper it tends to also become harder to train.
Larger training sets are also needed for deep networks, otherwise they can overfit
assertions.certainty_reason: An observation reported without evidence in the page.

assertions.value: The page states that backpropagation is the calculus-based strategy for updating weights, that its gradients can vanish or explode to impractically large values if not treated carefully, and that it sends updates from the output toward the input.
quotes: While in principle the rules of calculus give a simple strategy ( backpropagation ) to update the weights of the network
can either vanish or explode to impractically large values if not treated carefully.
as the name implies, backpropagation sends updates from the output toward the input.
assertions.certainty_reason: A general description without evidence in the page.

assertions.value: The page states that designing and training traditional networks requires substantial expertise and, even for experts, a significant amount of experimentation.
quotes: Designing and training traditional networks requires substantial expertise, and even for experts it requires a significant amount of experimentation.
assertions.certainty_reason: A general statement without evidence in the page.

assertions.value: The page states that training a single model can release the same amount of carbon as five cars during their lifetime, and that training neural networks is computationally expensive and uses a substantial amount of energy.
quotes: The process of training neural networks is also computationally expensive and uses a substantial amount of energy
Training a single model can release the same amount of carbon as five cars during their lifetime.
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited figure; the source is not named in the text layer.

assertions.value: The page states that training complicated models requires experimentation to set hyperparameters, and reports a case study in which choosing these parameters took almost 5,000 training cycles and multiplied the electricity consumption by a factor of nearly 2,000 compared to a single training cycle.
quotes: training of complicated models requires experimentation to determine the best hyperparameters
choosing these parameters took almost 5,000 training cycles of the network and multiplied the electricity consumption by a factor of nearly 2,000 compared to a single training cycle
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited case study in natural language processing networks; the source is not named in the text layer.
assertions.reader_inference: The page gives the number for a case study in networks commonly used in natural language processing; it is not a general figure for all networks.

assertions.value: The page states that in the reservoir approach most of the network is initialized randomly and never trained, and only a small, relatively simple fragment near the output is trained.
assertions.anchor: Minimizing training through the reservoir approach section, web page
quotes: In the reservoir approach, most of the network is initialized randomly and never trained.
Only a small, relatively simple, fragment of the network right near the output is ever trained.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page describes the reservoir approach as it defines it, in the Minimizing training section.

assertions.value: The page claims that the untrained part of a reservoir does not need to be tunable, which simplifies physical hardware implementation, and that the trained part sits by the output so no information is backpropagated through most of the network.
assertions.anchor: Minimizing training through the reservoir approach section, web page
quotes: The part that is not trained does not need to be tunable, which greatly simplifies implementation on physical hardware.
there is no need to backpropagate any information through most of the network
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describing the advantages of its own approach.

assertions.value: The page claims that the trained final part of a reservoir network can be shallow, so exploding or vanishing gradients are not a concern, and that it can even be linear because the untrained part expands the space and performs nonlinear transformations.
assertions.anchor: Minimizing training through the reservoir approach section, web page
quotes: The final trained part of the network can be shallow, so no need to worry about exploding or vanishing gradients.
since the untrained part of the network expands the space and performs nonlinear transformations, the part that is trained can even be linear.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describing the properties of its own approach.

assertions.value: The page states that the nonlinear interactions earlier in a reservoir machine mean it cannot be described as a simple matrix operation.
assertions.anchor: Minimizing training through the reservoir approach section, web page
quotes: The nonlinear interactions that occur earlier in a reservoir machine mean that it cannot be described as a simple matrix operation.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describing its own product.

assertions.value: The company claims that reservoir computers are much easier to train than other architectures, with fewer parameters and less work, that much less user expertise is needed, and that the multiplier on computational resources from experimentation is greatly reduced or even eliminated. The page reports no measurement for this claim.
assertions.anchor: Minimizing training through the reservoir approach section, web page
quotes: Effectively reservoir computers are just much easier to train than other architectures
much less expertise is needed from the user
the multiplier on computational resources coming from experimentation is greatly reduced or even eliminated
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describing its own product without measurement in the page.
assertions.reader_inference: The page offers no experiment comparing training cost of a reservoir with a traditional network.
